text:
Sam Kerr: Heads-up for the 18:00-22:00 UTC handoff — I'm primary until 18:15 UTC, then Priya takes primary. There's a 30m gap where we won't have a designated secondary listed (18:45-19:15 UTC) because Javier is stepping away. Can someone volunteer to shadow during that window?

Priya Nair: I can be on-call primary at 18:15. I can cover the shadow slot too if nobody else can, but prefer someone local to take the short interval.

Javier Moreno: Sorry, I need to step out for a maintenance call 18:45-19:15. I can be reachable by DM for quick confirm, but won't be actively paged.

Sam Kerr: Ok thanks. Two quick rules for this shift (please ack):
- If an alert hits P1 (customer-facing outage / >5% error-rate increase for >3min), page Primary immediately and escalate to Oncall Manager after 10m if not acknowledged.
- For degraded-but-not-outage (P2), page Primary only. If incident spans >30m with increasing impact, escalate to SRE Lead.

Tara Singh: Ack. Quick volunteer: I can shadow 18:45-19:15. Will mute unless escalated, but will monitor dashboards.

Sam Kerr: Perfect — Tara you’re the shadow for that window. Update rotation in the roster doc? I’ll add a note to the handoff doc.

incident-bot: ALERT (3752468120): high-req-latency detected on inference-prod-us-east - 99th p95 > 4000ms for 7 minutes. Severity candidate: P2. Links: https://grafana.redwood/dashboard/abc123

Priya Nair: seeing the alert. I’ll triage. First pass: check tail of serving logs and the autoscaler queue.

Sam Kerr: Triage checklist quick reference (run from infra console):
```
# check recent p95 trend
curl -s "https://metrics-api.redwood/series?m=p95&svc=inference-prod-us-east&range=15m" | jq .
# check autoscaler state
kubectl -n inference get hpa || kubectl -n inference describe deploy inference-service
# check recent errors
gcloud logging read "resource.type=container AND severity>=ERROR AND resource.labels.cluster_name=prod-us-east" --limit 50
```

Priya Nair: Results: autoscaler shows pending pods, some nodes at capacity. No spike in 5xx yet, just latency. Could be scheduling/queueing.

Javier Moreno: If it’s autoscaler backlog, temp mitigation = increase burst capacity via the reserved pool (if policy allows) or shift some traffic to the cheaper lower-latency region. Priya, do you have permission to trigger capacity burst?

Priya Nair: I do not. Policy requires approval from SRE Lead or Oncall Manager for reserved capacity burns > 2m GPUs.

Casey Lin: I’m SRE Lead — I can approve a 15m burst for this window. If you confirm it's autoscaler backlog, execute and monitor.

Sam Kerr: Escalation matrix (short):
- Page 1: Primary oncall (current primary) via pagerbot (Slack pings + phone).
- If no ack in 5m: Pager escalation to Secondary.
- If no resolution within 10m of page: escalate to Oncall Manager (casey@sre) + SRE Lead.
- If customer impact >30% sessions or >1 major customer affected: page exec on-call (via phone) and open incident bridge.

pagerbot: Paging Priya Nair -> primary oncall (page id: p-375246)

Priya Nair: Acked on pager. Initiating quick mitigation: adding ephemeral traffic split to eu-west for 10m to relieve us-east while Casey approves burst.

Tara Singh: Monitoring logs and request queues, nothing else anomalous in model loads.

Casey Lin: Approved capacity burst for 15m. Priority: scale inference-prod-us-east up by 4 GPUs, TTL 15m. If that doesn't reduce p95 within 3m, fallback to traffic-shift plan.

Priya Nair: Executed: requested 4 GPUs from reserved pool. Watching p95 now.

incident-bot: ACTION LOG (3752468148): capacity-burst request approved by Casey Lin, change-id cb-9981.

Sam Kerr: Customer impact assessment note: No wide customer errors yet. A few customers in us-east reported slower responses in the last 10m (CS tickets 6689, 6691). Keep CS updated every 15m until mitigated.

Priya Nair: p95 dropped from 4200ms -> 650ms in ~90s after burst. Looks like the burst helped. I'll leave the burst for full 15m then ramp back down.

Tara Singh: Good recovery observed. I’ll watch for flapping when we scale down. Recommend 5m cooldown before removing burst to allow warm-up.

Sam Kerr: Post-incident follow-ups:
- Add explicit secondary for 18:45-19:15 in the rota to avoid shadow gaps.
- Add a short runbook entry for "reserved-pool-burst" with exact approval flow and contact numbers. Link: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/reserved-pool-burst
- Add a snippet in handoff notes about temporary traffic-splits to other regions.

Javier Moreno: Thanks all. One ask: can we add a line in the handoff template reminding primaries to verify they have burst permissions or know who can approve? Saved me time asking.

Casey Lin: Good idea. I'll update the runbook. Also filing a retro ticket to review HPA thresholds vs. typical load spikes.

Priya Nair: All good from my side. If anything else flares up, page as per matrix.

Sam Kerr: Great work — Tara + Priya + Casey, thanks for jumping on. I'll update the roster and close this handoff thread. :thumbsup:
